notes: PT-BR per H.5's own recorded owner decision (2026-08-15) - cardinals0to99 extends the existing PORTUGUESE_CARDINALS_0_30 table verbatim for 0-20 and 30 (including the 21-29 space-wall exclusion), then continues to 99 - Portuguese has NO fused compounds anywhere in 21-99 (unlike Spanish's 'veintitres'): every non-round 2-digit value is space-linked via 'e'.

200-900 ARE single fused words when the remainder is exactly 0 ('duzentos'); a following remainder is 'e'-linked, unlike Spanish which uses a bare space with no connector word between hundred and the rest.
'quinhentos' (500) is irregular, not a regular '-centos' formation - listed explicitly, not derived.

IMPORTANT, NOT FULLY MODELED HERE: real Portuguese 'e'-placement across multiple magnitude levels is context-sensitive - 'e' appears before the FINAL element only when that element is < 100, and is OMITTED between two hundred-or-larger groups (e.g. 1234 = 'mil duzentos e trinta e quatro', with NO 'e' between 'mil' and 'duzentos' but an 'e' before 'trinta'). The remainderJoiner fields below give the word/joiner-type for each level; the exact recursive placement algorithm is Step 3's responsibility, not resolved by this data file - flagged explicitly so it isn't naively implemented as 'e' at every level.
Values whose composed reading contains a space are NOT representable by the FA tokenizer today - see scoped-in multi-word tokenizer extension.

yearReading.note: Portuguese has no pair-style year-reading convention - years are read as the full cardinal ('mil novecentos e noventa e oito'). Single real candidate - flagging for operator confirmation rather than assuming.
